content:
Warner Bros. announces it will test a new format for some iPhone users in the US: HBO Max Shorts. Vertical video is already annoying enough, and the media giant points out that these clips are powered by AI tools...

The company says AI is responsible for suggesting short clip content, with final decisions made by human editors.

"HBO Max Shorts" aims to present classic and memorable scenes from the HBO Max library in a vertical, swipeable interface to help users discover content they want to watch... These clips are powered by internally developed AI tools, using machine learning algorithms and scene-level metadata to sift through thousands of hours of footage, recommending the most engaging and impactful scenes for users to explore. After the AI tools make suggestions, HBO Max editors decide which ones best showcase audiences' favourite stories, then present them in a new vertical video format to ensure a smooth viewing experience.

Reportedly, content will be personalised based on each user's viewing history; if a user is interested in a particular short clip, they can start watching it immediately or add it directly to "My List" from the activity feed.

Warner Bros. says the feature is currently being tested with a small number of iPhone users in the US, but it appears the company has already decided to roll it out to other devices and markets later.
